title: Powers of ell act invertibly on derived continuous field coefficients
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed extension, and let $X$ be any scheme. Let $E_X=p_X^*\underline E$ be the actual continuous coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use internal module objects and their ordinary unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For every $K\in D(\Mod_{E_X})$ and every integer $n\geq0$, the endomorphism $\ell^n\operatorname{id}_K$ is invertible. The inverse is induced on a complex representative by the action of the constant coefficient $\ell^{-n}\in E$.

source.place: F inverts W: multiplication by ell on rational coefficients is invertible

proof.text: Put $a=\ell^n$ and $b=(\ell^n)^{-1}\in E$. Since $E$ contains $\mathbf Q_\ell$, $a\ne0$ and $ab=ba=1$. In the condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], the constant functions with values $a,b$ give sections $c_a,c_b:\mathbf Z\to\underline E$ of its underlying abelian ring object, with $c_ac_b=c_bc_a=1$. Here $c_t$ sends a locally constant integer-valued section $m$ to $m t$; these maps commute with restriction and satisfy the stated products pointwise. Pull them back to $E_X$ using the strong monoidal functor of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], obtaining sections $a_X,b_X$ with $a_Xb_X=b_Xa_X=1$. Also $a_X=\ell^n\cdot1$: the inverse image in [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] is a left adjoint between abelian sheaf categories, The adjunction identifies maps from $p_X^*(M\oplus N)$ to $G$ with pairs of maps from $p_X^*M,p_X^*N$ to $G$, and maps from $p_X^*0$ with the singleton; thus it preserves finite coproducts, zero objects and zero maps. In an abelian category these coproducts are biproducts, and addition is the composite of their diagonal, the two maps and the codiagonal; hence it preserves sums. Apply this to the finite sum $c_a=\ell^n c_1$.

source.place: F inverts W, sentence: ell acts invertibly on E_X-modules; expanded elementary inverse construction

proof.text: For any internal $E_X$-module $M$ with action $\gamma_M$, define $m_t(M)=\gamma_M\circ(t\otimes1_M)\circ\lambda_M^{-1}$ for $t=a_X,b_X$. The action axioms of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] give $m_s(M)m_t(M)=m_{st}(M)$ and $m_1(M)=1_M$. These are module morphisms: for a local ring section $r$ and module section $x$, $t(rx)=(tr)x=(rt)x=r(tx)$, since $E_X$ is commutative. Every module morphism $f:M\to N$ satisfies $f m_t(M)=m_t(N)f$ by its action-compatibility axiom. Thus, on any cochain complex $C$, the degreewise maps $A^q=m_{a_X}(C^q)$ and $B^q=m_{b_X}(C^q)$ commute with the differentials. They are chain maps with $AB=BA=1_C$. Additivity and unitality of the action give $A^q=\ell^n1_{C^q}$, hence $A=\ell^n1_C$.

source.place: F inverts W, sentence: ell acts invertibly on E_X-modules; expanded elementary inverse construction

proof.text: Use exactly the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\Mod_{E_X})$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. By [lem-sfb-derived-localization-additive], choose a cochain complex $C$ and an isomorphism $u:Q(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, and $Q$ is additive. Functoriality sends the two identities from step 2 to $Q(A)Q(B)=Q(B)Q(A)=1_{Q(C)}$. Additivity implies $Q(A)=Q(\ell^n1_C)=\ell^n1_{Q(C)}$, by induction on the finite sum of identities. Therefore $uQ(B)u^{-1}$ is a two-sided inverse of $uQ(A)u^{-1}=\ell^n1_K$. This is the claimed inverse induced by the constant coefficient $\ell^{-n}$. The formulas apply in every integer degree and require no boundedness condition.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement unchanged. Wrote the inverse via constant coefficient sections, the internal module action, and explicit inverse chain maps. One generic Mathlib leaf supplies additivity and essential surjectivity of the ordinary derived localization; no geometric comparison, finite rank, completion or boundedness result is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q31-21bc09563 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Item statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, and the item matches the blueprint thm-sfb-extend-scalars-localization proof l.12-13 ('ell acts invertibly on E_X-modules'). It has no repair note, it is not in route-pivot-dropped, live/side-live still show it unsplit, and no SGA source is cited. Step 1: the constant sections c_a, c_b: Z -> \underline E with pointwise products are transported along the strong monoidal p_X^*. p_X^* is a left adjoint between abelian categories, so it is additive and a_X = ell^n * unit (pullback-from-point (4)); this is elementary. Step 2: m_t = gamma(t (x) 1) lambda^{-1}. The action axioms give m_s m_t = m_st, the maps are module morphisms because E_X is commutative, and they commute with all module maps, so A and B are inverse chain maps with A = ell^n * 1. I checked this degreewise; it holds for unbounded complexes. Step 3: the new leaf gives a representative u: Q(C) = K and additivity of Q, so conjugating Q(B) gives the inverse on K. New leaf lem-sfb-derived-localization-additive: Mathlib DerivedCategory/Basic.lean l.146-147 (Q.Additive via additive_of_iso) and l.195-196 (Q.EssSurj) are exact, one declaration per clause.
